My name is not important, but I will tell you how I plan for my maize this season. My plot is small, only a little more than half a hectare, and here in Balaka the rains can be tricky — sometimes they come late or stop for weeks in January, so I cannot waste what I plant. I am hoping the coupon from the government will come again this year so I can buy a bag of NPK and a bag of urea at the cheap price; without that coupon, fertilizer at market price is too expensive for me. I will also carry the manure from my goats and the chicken droppings to the field before the rains, because even a little helps when the fertilizer is not enough. My husband helps some, but most of the weeding and planting I do myself with my children, and at weeding time if the grass is too much I may call one or two people for ganyu for a few days.
